image_description: A high-angle, close-up shot of a Nile crocodile partially submerged in murky brown water. The view focuses on the dorsal surface of the head and upper back, showcasing the rough, armored texture of the skin. The snout is visible at the bottom center, leading up to the neck and back which are covered in prominent osteoderms (scutes). There is significant splashing and water distortion around the upper portion of the animal.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers distinctly towards the nostrils, consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears anatomically correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal surface exhibits highly detailed, irregular but structured rows of bony scutes typical of crocodilian skin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs are visible in this specific crop/angle; they are either underwater or out of frame.
